title: To Get Smarter, Expand Your Inner Circle of Influence
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note argues that as leaders rise, their inner circle of trusted advisors tends to shrink even as their information intake grows, leaving them dependent on too few perspectives for critical decisions. The recommended fix is deliberately building a 'personal Board of Directors' -- expanding the number of trusted mentors and peers invited into important conversations. The piece includes practical advice on how to recruit these advisors and warns that failing to actually include them in real decisions will cause them to quietly disengage.
points: Leaders' trusted inner circles tend to shrink as they rise, even as their raw information intake increases.
The remedy proposed is a deliberate 'personal Board of Directors' of mentors and experienced peers.
Most experienced people are glad to be asked to serve as an additional sounding board if asked genuinely.
Mentors who are not actually included in real decisions will disengage or decline future invitations.
The piece frames a wider inner circle as directly producing better-quality decisions and strategy.
quotes: Leaders at the top of an organization are notorious for seeking loads of information from many sources, but for trusting only a few key people to help them think through difficult issues and problems.
If two heads are better than one, then 10 heads are a game changer.
People with great experience are commonly delighted to serve as an additional sounding board and source of perspective if they are asked in the right way.
The ultimate recognition for a mentor is to actively include them in the decision process on pressing issues.
Start today to build a personal Board of Directors that reflects a diverse set of viewpoints, experience, and wisdom.
